memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "These are the garments they are to make: a breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, a woven tunic, a turban and a sash. They are to make these sacred garments for your brother Aaron and his sons, so they may serve me as priests. Have them use gold, and blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and fine linen." - Exodus 28:4-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God lists the full set of garments — six pieces in all, made from gold thread, coloured yarn, and fine linen. The priest was covered from head to foot. Turban above, tunic and sash around, robe and ephod over, breastpiece at the heart. Nothing was left uncovered or unaddressed.

The repeated phrase tells us the purpose: "so they may serve me as priests." Every single item existed for service. These were working clothes, not display pieces. The beauty was real, but it was beauty in the service of function. Aaron wore all of this in order to do something — to represent the people before God.

That reframes how we think about what God gives us. Our gifts, our resources, our position, even our appearance — none of it is given merely for display. It is given for service. Paul writes that each has received a gift and should use it to serve others, as faithful stewards of God's grace (1 Pet 4:10). Ask yourself today not "what do I have?" but "what is it for?" God clothes His people in order to send them out to serve.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I treating God's gifts to me as display or as equipment for service?
What has God given me that He is asking me to put to use for others?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, everything You have given me is meant for service, not display. Show me how to use what I have to serve others faithfully as a steward of Your grace. Amen.
